newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: One dead, two hurt in Cambodian TV station attack.
newsitem.headline: One dead, two hurt in Cambodian TV station attack.

text.p: Unidentified gunmen killed an announcer and wounded two others during an overnight grenade attack on a state-run television studio in southern Cambodia, police said on Monday.

Officials feared the attack marked a fresh escalation in the bitter row between the country's two leading parties in the ailing coalition government, the royalist FUNCINPEC party and the Cambodian People's Party.
Seven men went to the studio in the southern port city of Sihanoukville on Sunday night and opened fire with AK-47 assault rifles and rocket-propelled grenades.
Two announcers were seriously wounded and transmission equipment destroyed, Sihanoukville police chief Em Bunsath said by telephone. A guard was slightly wounded.
He said one of the announcers, Pith Em, died in hospital at 0740 GMT on Monday.
Em Bunsath, a member of the royalist FUNCINPEC party, said an investigation had been launched.
Secretary of State for Information Khieu Kanarith had travelled to Sihanoukville to help investigate, officials said.
Em Bunsath said the attack might be political because there were no signs of robbery.

An Interior Ministry official, who asked not to be identified, said the FUNCINPEC party had days earlier asked the Sihanoukville branch of state television to broadcast a speech by one of its top officials attacking the Cambodian People's Party.
Armed men later went to the house of the station chief and made the same demand. The station chief refused.
FUNCINPEC and the Cambodian People's Party formed an uneasy coalition government after U.N.-run elections in 1993.
Relations deteriorated dramatically after a deadly March 30 grenade attack on a rally led by opposition leader and FUNCINPEC ally Sam Rainsy.
FUNCINPEC has complained that is not being given the same amount of air time on state-run media as the Cambodian People's Party.
